changed.title: Row containment through a dominating wire on the one-a-side promise for AND/OR gates of fan-in at most two reading earlier wires
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (u v : Fin n) (O : ℕ),
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  u ≠ v →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length) u.val = 1 →
  C.output ≠ u.val →
  O < n + m + C.gates.length →
  (∀ c : Fin m, (C.wires (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach v c)).getD O false = true) →
  (¬ Relation.TransGen
    (fun a b : ℕ => a ≠ O ∧ b ≠ O ∧
      ∃ j : Fin C.gates.length, b = n + m + j.val ∧
        a ∈ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C j.val).inputs)
    u.val C.output) →
  ∀ c : Fin m, G u c = true → G v c = true
changed.unlocks: a tool for the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise, used where every row is read once by an OR; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. Fix a column c. Call a wire safe if every operand path to it from the input for row u passes through O, the empty path counted. O is on at (v, c). Every other safe input wire has value at (u, c) at most its value at (v, c). For a safe gate other than O all operands are safe, since a path avoiding O would extend to the gate. Induct along earlier wires: AND and OR are monotone, so each safe wire's value at (u, c) is at most its value at (v, c). The output is safe; apply this there and use that the circuit represents the graph. An absent output reads false.
